newsitem.title: USA: Compaq cuts some commercial prices.
newsitem.headline: Compaq cuts some commercial prices.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp said Tuesday it lowered U.S. prices on several commercial desktop personal computers by up to 23 percent and prices on related desktop options, including memory and the Compaq Scanner Keyboard, by up to 53 percent.
Prices were lowered on existing inventory of select Compaq ProLinea and Deskpro desktop PC models, the company said.

For example, it said, the Compaq Deskpro 5150 Model 1200 featuring a Pentium 150-megahertz processor, 16 megabytes of memory and a large 1.2-gigabyte hard drive is expected to sell for $1,825, a $330 reduction.
The Compaq Scanner Keyboard, which integrates paper-driven document scanning with a Windows 95-based keyboard, now sells for $299, a reduction of eight percent, Compaq said.

"This pricing action also enhances our reseller partners' selling efforts. In particular, memory option sales continue to be a strong revenue and margin opportunity for Compaq resellers due to the momentum of Microsoft Windows 95 and Windows NT which require 16 megabytes or more of memory to run optimally," Compaq explained.
